Emily —

Appreciate the clear list. We can provide an evidence packet that covers everything you asked for. High-level answers below and attachments to follow in a separate email. If anything needs deeper technical detail, Neha (our security lead) will jump in.

- TLS in transit: Public hosted API endpoints enforce TLS 1.2 minimum; we prefer TLS 1.3 where supported. Cipher suites prioritized: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256, ECDHE-based suites for RSA fallback. (See attached tls_cipher_config_snippet.txt)
- KMS/HSM: For Redwood-hosted tenants, CMKs are HSM-backed via our cloud provider KMS (HSM root of trust). For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS/HSM (BYOK) or we can deploy a customer-controlled KMS in their VPC. CMKs are marked non-exportable in hosted and dedicated modes unless configured explicitly in Private BYOK scenarios.
- HSM vendor & attestation: We leverage cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM / Google Cloud HSM) and maintain the vendor attestations; we are attaching the most recent HSM attestation we can share.
- Key rotation: We maintain automated rotation of ephemeral data keys on a 90-day cadence; CMKs have a configurable rotation policy and we recommend annual rotation for master keys. We are attaching a short rotation log excerpt that shows the last CMK rotation timestamp for the production key (see kms_rotation_log_excerpt.csv).

We'll put the artifacts together (attestation PDF, rotation log CSV excerpt, TLS config snippet, and a short diagram) and send them in one packet. Can you do Mon 11/16 13:00 ET for a 30-min call? That slot works for us.

Emily / team —

Adding the technical specifics you asked for and clarifying a couple of deployment distinctions:

1) At-rest encryption
- Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256-GCM. Object-storage and database volumes use envelope encryption with data keys (DEKs) protected by CMKs.
- For hosted (Redwood-managed) deployments: CMKs are generated and stored in cloud KMS with HSM-backed key material; CMKs are configured non-exportable.
- For Dedicated and Private: customers can opt for BYOK with customer-controlled KMS (HSM-backed) in their account/VPC. We also support HSM-backed key import via PKCS#11 for some private/on-prem configs.

2) In-transit
- API endpoints terminate TLS at the load balancer and enforce TLS 1.2+ with TLS 1.3 preferred. We support modern cipher suites; the attached tls_cipher_config_snippet.txt contains the active cipher list served for public endpoints.

3) KMS / HSM details and rotation
- HSM provider: we use the cloud provider HSM (AWS CloudHSM or Google Cloud HSM) for Redwood-managed CMKs; for customer BYOK we accept keys from AWS KMS, Google KMS, and external HSM via PKCS#11 depending on deployment.
- Non-exportability: Redwood-managed CMKs are non-exportable by design. BYOK keys are controlled by the customer and may have different export policies depending on their HSM/provider.
- Rotation policy: DEKs are rotated automatically every 90 days; CMKs have configurable rotation: default is annual rotation for CMKs; customers can enable more frequent rotation for their BYOK.
- Last rotation timestamps (production/root CMK): 2026-10-30T02:00:00Z (rotation completed, automated job), see kms_rotation_log_excerpt.csv for audit entries showing the rotation action id and service principal.

4) Auditability
- Audit logs: rotation actions, key usage (Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign) are logged to our centralized audit pipeline and retained per contract (default 90 days, configurable). We can provide a redacted excerpt of the rotation audit showing key IDs and timestamps.

I have attached the items below. Note the HSM attestation we can share is vendor-supplied and redacted for vendor/customer IDs where required. If you need an official signed attestation from Redwood, we can prepare a short attestation letter for signature — please indicate whether Big Bank requires that.
